summary: Stack-local builder that collects sprite-part records (20-, 40- and 44-byte flavours) plus the transform for one sprite instance; created by Gfx_Scene_CreateSpritePart14/40 and consumed by Gfx_Scene_CreateSpriteInstance.
evidence: Ctor 0x0058C40C (inlined into Gfx_Scene_CreateSpritePart40 0x002E77CC, which passes the stack block auStack_bc..local_28 = 0x94 bytes) writes byte +0=1, zeroes +4..+0xc, copies 20 floats of default transform into +0x10..+0x5f, then three {begin,end,capacityEnd,allocator} vector triples at +0x64/+0x74/+0x84. Gfx_SpriteParts_Clear (0x0058C4A0) releases all three through the allocator vtable slot +0x14.

fields.name: dirtyFlags
fields.evidence: Gfx_PartList_AppendRecord20/44 and Gfx_SpriteParts_AppendRecord all do *(u32*)(parts+0x60) |= 2 before appending; ctor zeroes it.

fields.name: part20End
fields.evidence: Write cursor of the 20-byte record vector: AppendRecord20 stores at parts->f_68 then advances it by 0x14; Clear walks f_64..f_68 in 0x14 steps.

fields.name: part20CapacityEnd
fields.evidence: AppendRecord20 grows the vector when f_6c <= f_68 (std_Vector20_Reserve on parts+0x64); Clear zeroes it.

fields.name: part20Allocator
fields.evidence: Ctor stores the incoming allocator argument here; Clear calls (*(*f_70)+0x14)(...) to free the 20-byte vector.

fields.name: part40Begin
fields.evidence: Base pointer of the 40-byte record vector: std_Vector40_Reserve((int*)&parts->f_74, ...) and Clear walks f_74..f_78 in 0x28 steps.

fields.name: part40End
fields.evidence: Write cursor of the 40-byte vector: Gfx_SpriteParts_AppendRecord stores ten words at f_78 then advances it by 0x28.

fields.name: part40CapacityEnd
fields.evidence: AppendRecord grows when f_7c <= f_78; Clear zeroes it.

fields.name: part40Allocator
fields.evidence: Ctor stores the allocator argument here; Clear frees the 40-byte vector through (*(*f_80)+0x14).

fields.name: part44Begin
fields.evidence: Base pointer of the 44-byte record vector: std_Vector44_Reserve((int*)&parts->f_84, ...) and Clear walks f_84..f_88 in 0x2c steps.

fields.name: part44End
fields.evidence: Write cursor of the 44-byte vector: Gfx_PartList_AppendRecord44 stores eleven words at f_88 then advances it by 0x2c.

fields.name: part44CapacityEnd
fields.evidence: AppendRecord44 grows when f_8c <= f_88; Clear zeroes it.

fields.name: part44Allocator
fields.evidence: Ctor stores the allocator argument here; Clear frees the 44-byte vector through (*(*f_90)+0x14).

fields.name: unknown_8e4
fields.evidence: Misattributed: the only evidence line is *(u8*)(*param_1 + 0x239) = value from Gfx_SpriteParts_SetFlag239 (0x0047AF5C), where param_1 is a GfxSpritePart** array and +0x239 belongs to the pointed-to part, not to this builder. 0x239*4 = 0x8e4 explains the bogus offset; the real object is 0x94 bytes.

summary: Billboard (descriptor type 1) effect emitter: one non-rotated sprite child whose scale is the definition radius times the shared basis vector, plus the definition colour and ids.
evidence: Effect_BillboardEmitter_Setup (0x0040EB90) is the only recovered method: it stores the definition colour into +0x9c..+0xa4 and mirrors it into +0x2c8..+0x2d0, sets the layer byte +0x274 into the sprite descriptor, and attaches one child through Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChildC(self, desc, &self->f_278, 0).

fields.name: positionX
fields.evidence: Gfx_Node +0x9c is the first component of the node position (Gfx_Node_Ctor 0x005F8178 copies the 8-float block 0x007E719C into +0x88..+0xa4; S_045 named +0x8c..+0x98 quaternion and +0x9c..+0xa4 position). Setup stores def[5] here.

fields.name: positionY
fields.evidence: Second position component; Setup stores def[6] here.

fields.name: positionZ
fields.evidence: Third position component; Setup stores def[7] here.

fields.name: maybe_isVisible
fields.evidence: Gfx_Node_Ctor sets +0x118=1, +0x119=1, +0x11a=0 as three consecutive flag bytes and every emitter setup re-sets +0x118=1; no reader was recovered, so the exact flag is unproven.

fields.name: maybe_definitionLayer
fields.evidence: Setup copies one definition byte here (def+0x10); the same offset is a 0xFF-terminated id in Field_SceneObject/Field_Prop and a definition byte in Gfx_ModelPart, so the exact meaning is unproven.

fields.name: layer
fields.evidence: Read into local_32 and stored as the sprite child descriptor's layer byte before Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChildC; Gfx_SpriteActor and Gfx_ModelPart read the same offset the same way.

fields.name: childList
fields.evidence: Passed as the attach node argument of Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChildC(self, desc, &self->f_278, 0).

fields.name: maybe_originX
fields.evidence: Setup copies positionX (+0x9c) here; the same offset holds unrelated data in the sibling emitter classes, so this is a per-class snapshot of the spawn position.

fields.name: maybe_originY
fields.evidence: Setup copies positionY (+0xa0) here.

fields.name: maybe_originZ
fields.evidence: Setup copies positionZ (+0xa4) here.

fields.name: maybe_subIdByte
fields.evidence: Setup copies the definition byte at def+0x2e here; the sibling setups store a definition byte at the same offset.

fields.name: maybe_subIdWord
fields.evidence: Setup copies the definition u16 at def+0xb here.

Field_Level_InitSpriteSets (0x00610890) calls it at levelWork+0x98 and the next container Gfx_SceneSpriteSet_Create at +0x7c later, so the object is 0x7c bytes.

fields.evidence: Zeroed by Create; no reader recovered.

fields.name: maybe_handle58
fields.evidence: Create stores 0xFFFFF000 (invalid-handle sentinel).

fields.name: maybe_flag5e

fields.name: layer
fields.evidence: Read into local_42 and stored as the sprite child descriptor's layer byte before Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChildC.

fields.name: childList
fields.evidence: Attach node argument of Gfx_SpriteActor_AddChildC(self, desc, &self->f_278, 0).

fields.name: maybe_definitionByte2c7
fields.evidence: Setup copies the definition byte at def+0x49 here; no reader recovered.

fields.evidence: Setup writes 0xFF then 0/1/2/3 depending on which of the four (count, offset) pairs is non-empty; the group index selects the particle variant.

fields.name: maybe_definitionByte2d0

summary: 2D effect manager: 33 pack slots of 0x10 bytes at +0x34, a pack-info-entry to slot table at +0x244, the manager pack at +0x2fc/+0x300 and two intrusive instance lists.
evidence: Gfx_Effect2D_Shutdown (0x003DBD60) loops i=0..0x20 over slots at self+i*0x10 with refcount +0x34, pack handle +0x38, pack-info +0x3c and pack-info handle +0x40, then memsets the 0xB5-byte table at +0x244 to 0xFF and releases +0x300. Gfx_Effect2D_AcquireSlot (0x003DBBDC) formats 'effect2d/%s.pack' and writes the slot index into +0x244.

fields.name: activeListHead
fields.evidence: Gfx_Effect2D_DeleteAll (0x003DB8A8) walks the active-instance list until *node == self->f_10, i.e. this word is the list sentinel address.

fields.name: activeListFirst
fields.evidence: First node of the active-instance list in Gfx_Effect2D_DeleteAll.

fields.name: pendingListHead
fields.evidence: Sentinel of the second (pending) instance list in Gfx_Effect2D_DeleteAll.

fields.name: pendingListFirst
fields.evidence: First node of the pending instance list in Gfx_Effect2D_DeleteAll.

fields.name: commonPackRefCount
fields.evidence: Slot 0 refcount: Gfx_Effect2D_LoadCommonPack sets it to 1, AcquireSlot searches slots 1..0x20 only, ReleasePack decrements it.

fields.name: commonPackHandle
fields.evidence: Slot 0 pack handle: Pack_HandlePair_MoveAssign(&self->f_38, ...) in LoadCommonPack, Pack_ReleaseHandleEntry(&self->f_38) in ReleasePack.

fields.name: commonPackInfo
fields.evidence: Slot 0 pack-info record: Gfx_Effect2D_AttachPackInfo stores the resolved 'effect2d_packinfo.epi' object at iVar1->f_3c and reads its entry count at +0x84.

fields.name: commonPackInfoHandle
fields.evidence: Slot 0 pack-info handle: Pack_HandlePair_MoveAssign(&iVar1->f_40, ...) in AttachPackInfo, Pack_ReleaseHandleEntry(&iVar7->f_40) in ReleaseSlot.

fields.name: slotIndexByEntry
fields.evidence: 0xB5-byte table: AttachPackInfo writes the slot index for every pack-info entry, ReleaseSlot/ReleasePack write 0xFF, Shutdown memsets it to 0xFF; AcquireSlot reads it as the slot of a list index.

fields.name: managerPack
fields.evidence: Gfx_Effect2D_LoadManagerPack stores the pack record here after checking its pack-info id is 0xB5; AcquireSlot/ReleaseSlot read its entry count at +0x60 and its offset table at +0x58.

fields.name: managerPackHandle
fields.evidence: Pack_HandlePair_MoveAssign(&self->f_300, ...) in LoadManagerPack, Pack_ReleaseHandleEntry(&self->f_300) in Shutdown/ReleasePack.

summary: Shared 0x60-byte sprite draw context used as the header of every scene sprite object: vtable, default params, scene resource, four sprite pools and a 0x34-byte quad block at +0x1c.
evidence: Gfx_Scene_SpriteCtx_Init (0x002E7F5C) has 60 callers (Field_NpcMoveTowardTarget, Ui_LayoutParams_Init, Camera_UpdateWorkPath, ...), so it is a shared base initialiser: it stores vtable 0x007611F8 at +0, the rodata object 0x00782234 at +4, zeroes +8..+0x18, runs func_00588430(self+0x1c) for the 0x34-byte quad block and zeroes +0x50..+0x5c.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Init stores the rodata pointer 0x007611F8 at +0; Gfx_Sprite derives from this class.

fields.name: defaultParams
fields.evidence: Init stores the rodata object 0x00782234, which 292 functions reference as a shared default descriptor.

fields.name: unknown_08
fields.evidence: Zeroed by Init; Gfx_Sprite's ctor copies a source word here. No reader recovered.

fields.name: unknown_0c
fields.evidence: Zeroed by Init; Gfx_Sprite's ctor stores a ctor argument here. No reader recovered.

fields.name: unknown_10
fields.evidence: Zeroed by Init; Gfx_Sprite's ctor stores a ctor argument here. No reader recovered.

fields.name: scene
fields.evidence: Gfx_Scene_DrawSprite (0x002E58E0) passes self->f_14 as the scene resource to the draw entry; Gfx_Scene_RemoveSpriteEntries uses self->f_14->f_2c.

fields.name: spriteSlotPool
fields.evidence: Gfx_Scene_RemoveSpriteEntries reads capacity +0xc, data +4, bitmap +8 and live count +0x10 from self->f_18 and indexes 0x34-byte entries.

fields.name: spriteEntryPool
fields.evidence: Gfx_Scene_AddSpriteEntryLarge/Small read self->f_50->f_c (capacity) and *(int*)(f_50+4) (data) and index 0x40-byte entries; AddNodeType1/2 look entries up with func_007141A8(self->f_50, handle & 0xffff).

fields.name: nodeAllocator
fields.evidence: Gfx_Scene_AddNodeType1/2 pass self->f_54 to func_00707E98 to allocate the node record.

fields.name: spriteBitmapPool
fields.evidence: Gfx_Scene_AllocSpriteSlot walks the inverted bitmap at self->f_58 (capacity +0xc, data +4, bitmap +8, live count +0x10) and indexes 0x24-byte entries.

fields.name: spritePool
fields.evidence: Gfx_Scene_AllocSpritePoolHandle forwards self->f_5c to Gfx_SpritePool_Alloc (0x005F24A4) and returns entry->u32_68.

summary: Follow/trail effect attached to an actor: spawns effect 1237 (moving) or 1238 (standing) at the owner's position when it moves, and tracks the effect handle and the owner model.
evidence: Effect_ActorTrail_Ctor (0x004A650C) runs base init 0x002D97E8, overwrites the vtable with 0x007757A0 and sets +0x3c=0, +0x40=0xFFFFFC00, +0x44=0x0076B690, +0x48=0, +0x4c=+0x38. Effect_ActorTrail_Update (0x004A60CC) gates on +0x10, reads the owner model at +0x38 and spawns through Effect_FindOrCreateInstance. The batch size 228 comes from the misattributed +0xe0 entry; the real object is 0x54 bytes (Effect_ActorTrailVariant is exactly 84).

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Ctor stores 0x007757A0; the batch vtable 0x007757A4 holds ReleaseInstance/Update/Stop/ShouldFinish.

fields.name: isActive
fields.evidence: Effect_ActorTrail_Update returns immediately when this byte is 0; Effect_ActorTrail_Stop releases the handle and clears it.

fields.name: ownerActor
fields.evidence: Update reads the model id at owner+0x170, the position at +0x9c..+0xa4, the previous position at +0xc0..+0xc8 and the quaternion at +0x8c..+0x98; ShouldFinish tests owner->f_51.

fields.name: moveState
fields.evidence: Update writes 1 when the owner moved less than 0.0009 squared units and 2 when it moved further; the value selects effect id 0x4d5 or 0x4d6.

fields.name: effectHandle
fields.evidence: Ctor stores 0xFFFFFC00 (invalid); Update stores the handle returned by Effect_FindOrCreateInstance; ReleaseInstance/Stop validate it against the handle table 0x007B4D68 and call Effect_ReleaseHandle.

fields.name: effectLinkVtable
fields.evidence: Ctor stores 0x0076B690 here; func_001CF7F8(self+0x44) stamps 0x00759D34 over it and clears the instance back-pointer, so +0x44/+0x48 form a 2-word link struct.

fields.name: effectInstance
fields.evidence: Ctor zeroes it; Effect_FindOrCreateInstance writes the new instance to *(type+4) where type = &self->f_44, i.e. this word.

fields.name: maybe_prevOwnerActor
fields.evidence: Ctor zeroes it and then copies +0x38 (ownerActor) into it; no reader recovered, so it is probably a previous-owner snapshot.

fields.name: childEffect
fields.evidence: Effect_ActorTrail_ShouldFinishB (0x00655234) keeps the trail alive while self->f_50 is non-null and its byte +0x312 is 0.

fields.name: unknown_e0
fields.evidence: Misattributed: the evidence line is (**(code**)(*param_1 + 0x38))(param_1), a vtable slot 0x38 call; 0x38*4 = 0xe0 explains the bogus offset. Not a field.

summary: Movie demux/feed pump: holds the demuxer, the output sink, per-track state and the audio/video feed counters.
evidence: Gfx_MovieDecoder_FeedVideo (0x004FED80) and FeedAudio (0x004FEEF4) drive the demuxer at +0x18, index per-track arrays with +0x560 and submit to the sink at +0x1d8; CheckEndOfStream (0x004FF278) moves the state at +0xc to 7 (failed) or 8 (finished).

fields.name: state
fields.evidence: CheckEndOfStream compares it with 0/1/3/4 and writes 7 (error) or 8 (end of stream); FeedAudio moves 5 -> 3 when the streams are drained.

fields.name: demuxer
fields.evidence: Every demuxer call dereferences it: Gfx_Movie_GetReadyFrame(*self->f_18, ...), func_006B99B8(*self->f_18, ...), func_006B9BF4(*self->f_18).

fields.name: startTimeLow
fields.evidence: FeedVideo latches local_28 here when both +0x148 and +0x14c are still 0, i.e. the first frame's timestamp.

fields.name: startTimeHigh
fields.evidence: Second half of the latched first-frame timestamp (see +0x148).

fields.name: outputSink
fields.evidence: FeedVideo calls (*(*self->f_1d8 + 8))(self->f_1d8, surface, size) and aborts the pump when it returns 0.

fields.name: maybe_videoTrackCount
fields.evidence: FeedVideo only runs when 0 < self->f_49c; no other use recovered, so it is probably the number of video tracks.

fields.name: currentVideoTrack
fields.evidence: Indexes the per-track arrays: +0x540 (u32), +0x4a0 (pointer), +0x4c4 (int, stride 0x10); FeedAudio also tests it before func_006B98B4.

fields.name: maybe_streamStarted
fields.evidence: FeedVideo calls the sink's vtable slot +0x10 only while this byte is 0, sets it to 1, and clears it after each submitted frame.

fields.name: audioFrameCount
fields.evidence: FeedAudio adds the number of audio frames consumed (local_54) to it on every submitted sample.

fields.name: audioByteCount
fields.evidence: FeedAudio adds the sample size returned by func_006B99B8 (local_38[3]) to it on every submitted sample.

fields.evidence: Setup stores the definition pointer itself here (*(void**)(self+0x2c8) = def), unlike the sibling emitters which store a value.

summary: Two-batch draw packet: vertex format id, the two batch headers, the allocated vertex buffer and the allocator that owns it.
evidence: Gfx_DrawPacket_BuildFormat1/2/3 (0x0058CAF0/0x0058C580/0x0058C758) all set packet[3] to the format id 1/2/3, packet[2] to the buffer returned by Gfx_DrawPacket_ResizeBuffer, packet[0]/packet[1] to the two batch headers and packet[4] to one parameter word; Gfx_DrawPacket_Release (0x0058CA98) frees through packet[5]'s vtable slot +0x14 and zeroes all eight words.

fields.name: batchA
fields.evidence: BuildFormat1/2/3 store the first 0x40-byte batch header here (*packet = puVar4).

fields.name: batchB
fields.evidence: BuildFormat1/2/3 store the second batch header here (packet[1] = puVar4).

fields.name: packetData
fields.evidence: BuildFormat1/2/3 store the buffer returned by Gfx_DrawPacket_ResizeBuffer here (packet[2]).

fields.name: vertexFormat
fields.evidence: BuildFormat1 writes 1, BuildFormat2 writes 2, BuildFormat3 writes 3, Release writes 0.

fields.name: maybe_paramWord
fields.evidence: BuildFormat2 stores params[3] and BuildFormat3 stores params[7] here; the choice depends on the vertex format, so the exact meaning is unproven.

fields.name: allocator
fields.evidence: Gfx_DrawPacket_ResizeBuffer calls (*(*packet->f_14 + 0x14))(alloc, old) to free and (*(*packet->f_14 + 0xc))(alloc, 4, bytes) to allocate.

fields.name: bufferData
fields.evidence: ResizeBuffer stores the newly allocated block here and Release frees it through the allocator.

fields.name: bufferCapacity
fields.evidence: ResizeBuffer compares it with the requested byte count and stores the new size after reallocating.

summary: Ring buffer of decoded movie frames: two parallel per-slot arrays, read/write indices and the queued count, all guarded by the global movie monitor 0x007CF360.
evidence: Gfx_MovieQueue_Push (0x006B95E4) writes the converted surface into f_28[tail] and its paired value into f_2c[tail], advances f_30 modulo the capacity at +8 and increments f_38; Gfx_MovieQueue_Pop (0x006B9518) advances f_34 and decrements f_38; maybe_Gfx_MovieQueue_Peek (0x006B93A4) copies the descriptor out without advancing f_34.

fields.name: maybe_frameTimestamp
fields.evidence: maybe_Gfx_MovieQueue_Peek (0x006B93A4) copies this word into three consecutive output descriptor slots (out[3..5]); no other use recovered, so it is a per-queue frame word of unknown exact meaning (timestamp is the most likely reading).

fields.name: maybe_frameTime
fields.evidence: Peek copies it into out[6]; no other use recovered.

fields.name: maybe_frameDuration
fields.evidence: Peek copies it into out[7]; no other use recovered.

fields.name: frameEntries
fields.evidence: Per-slot u32 array: Push stores the converted surface at f_28[tail], Peek reads f_28[readIndex].

fields.name: frameTimestamps
fields.evidence: Second per-slot u32 array: Push stores the value from func_0015D4A0 at f_2c[tail], Peek reads f_2c[readIndex].

fields.name: writeIndex
fields.evidence: Push increments it and wraps it at the capacity in +8.

fields.name: readIndex
fields.evidence: Pop increments it and wraps it at the capacity in +8; Peek reads it without advancing.

fields.name: count
fields.evidence: Queued frame count: Push increments, Pop decrements, GetCount returns it, Push refuses when it reaches the capacity.

summary: Movie decoder worker thread object: a state machine (1 idle, 3 running, 5 starting, 6 stopping), a mutex, two 64-bit tick accumulators and the last stop stamp.
evidence: Gfx_MovieThread_Stop (0x004FE88C) moves 3 -> 6 and stamps svcGetSystemTick/1000 into +0x168; Start (0x004FE94C) moves to 5 and waits for 3; Join (0x004FE9D4) moves 6 -> 5 -> 3 and adds the elapsed ticks to +0x150 and +0x158. All three take Os_LockMonitor(self) and Os_MutexLock(&self->f_20).

fields.name: state
fields.evidence: Stop tests 6 and 3 and writes 6; Start tests 1/8 and writes 5, waits for 3; Join tests 6, writes 5, waits for 3; 7 is the failure state.

fields.name: mutex
fields.evidence: Os_MutexLock(&self->f_20) in Start and Join guards the state transition.

fields.name: totalTicksLow
fields.evidence: Low word of a 64-bit accumulator: Join does self->f_150 = delta + f150 and self->f_154 = carry + f154 + carry(f150,delta).

fields.name: totalTicksHigh
fields.evidence: High word of the +0x150 accumulator (carry-propagating add in Join).

fields.name: maybe_secondTicksLow
fields.evidence: Low word of a second 64-bit accumulator that receives the same delta as +0x150 in Join; the difference between the two counters is not recovered.

fields.name: maybe_secondTicksHigh
fields.evidence: High word of the +0x158 accumulator.

fields.name: lastStopTickLow
fields.evidence: Low word of the 64-bit tick stamp: Stop stores the 64-bit result of std_Int64MulDiv(tick,1000) here, Join subtracts it from the current tick to get the delta.

fields.name: lastStopTickHigh
fields.evidence: High word of the +0x168 tick stamp (Join's 64-bit subtraction reads it).
